definitions.explanation: A general term for any tool with a cutting edge, including knives, scissors, razors, and swords.

examples.japanese: {刃物|はもの}の{取|と}り{扱|あつか}いに{注意|ちゅうい}する。
examples.english: Be careful when handling bladed tools.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{手|て}の{届|とど}く{場所|ばしょ}に{刃物|はもの}を{置|お}かないでください。
examples.english: Please don't leave sharp objects within children's reach.

examples.japanese: {堺|さかい}は{古|ふる}くから{刃物|はもの}の{産地|さんち}として{知|し}られており、{今|いま}でも{高品質|こうひんしつ}な{包丁|ほうちょう}が{作|つく}られている。
examples.english: Sakai has been known as a production center for bladed tools since ancient times, and high-quality kitchen knives are still made there today.

notes:
Compound of {刃|は} (blade, cutting edge) + {物|もの} (thing). A broad category term covering all cutting tools.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{刃物|はもの}を{持|も}つ (to carry a blade)
・{刃物|はもの}の{産地|さんち} (blade-making region)
・{刃物|はもの}の{手入|てい}れ (maintenance of blades)
・{刃物|はもの}を{研|と}ぐ (to sharpen a blade)

WHAT COUNTS AS {刃物|はもの}:
・{包丁|ほうちょう} (kitchen knife)
・はさみ (scissors)
・カッター (box cutter)
・{剃刀|かみそり} (razor)
・{鎌|かま} (sickle)
・{刀|かたな} (sword)

USAGE NOTES:
{堺|さかい} (in {大阪|おおさか}) and {関|せき} (in {岐阜|ぎふ}) are famous production areas for Japanese {刃物|はもの}. In safety contexts, {刃物|はもの} is used generically for any sharp cutting tool.
